feed.title: Lab Canary: rating updates
feed.subtitle: Changes to Lab Canary's ratings of what's publicly known about AI lab staff contracts, speak-up policies and contracts with outside evaluators.

entry.title: OpenAI: new speak-up policy sends AI safety concerns to a board committee
entry.summary: OpenAI replaced its Raising Concerns Policy on 30 October 2026. Staff can now take an AI safety concern straight to the Safety and Security Committee of the OpenAI Foundation's board, safety concerns raised through the anonymous Integrity Line are passed to that committee, and the policy says the committee has "full authority" to address them. "Safe internal channel" moves from B to A, so OpenAI's score goes from 43% to 46%. "Protected disclosures carved out" stays a C: the policy now covers former staff, but it still says it isn't a contract and doesn't say that no agreement overrides it.

entry.title: Anthropic: IPO filing makes its staff stock plan public
entry.summary: Anthropic filed to go public on 26 October 2026, and the filing includes its staff stock plan. The plan says anyone fired "for Cause" loses all their unexercised stock options and all their restricted stock units, vested ones included. "Cause" includes "intentional material damage to the Company's business, property or reputation", and the company's decision on it is "final and binding". "Equity is never hostage" now cites the plan and stays a D: the plan has no stated exception for criticism or protected disclosures, but losing equity under it takes a for-Cause firing. "Protected disclosures carved out" also cites a severance agreement for executives from the same filing and stays a B. Scores are unchanged.

entry.title: Google DeepMind: former staff say raising the non-disparagement clause through formal routes changed nothing
entry.summary: "Safe internal channel" now cites two accounts. Former research engineer Sofia Liguori told openDemocracy that an employee's attempts to raise the clause through internal channels led to no change. Andreas Kirsch has said he raised it in a formal protected disclosure in September 2026 and nothing changed, IBTimes UK reported. The grade stays a D. "Protected disclosures carved out" now notes that UK law voids a contract term so far as it tries to stop a protected disclosure, and stays "Not public". Scores are unchanged.

entry.title: xAI is now listed as xAI / SpaceXSI
entry.summary: xAI now calls itself SpaceXSI (SpaceX Super Intelligence LLC); its terms of service, last updated on 27 October 2026, use that name. The scorecard now lists it as "xAI / SpaceXSI". Its page links and feed address changed with the name, and the old feed address redirects to the new one. No grade changed: "Whistleblowing policy is public" stays an F.

entry.title: Grades now run from A to F
entry.summary: "Partly" was covering too much: 11 of the 17 ratings on staff contracts were "Partly", including all six of Anthropic's. Each clause is now split into three or four parts. "Meets" is an A and "Falls short" is an F. "Partly" is split into B (one part missing), C (in between) and D (only one part shown). "Not public" shows as "?" and still scores zero. A scores 1, B three quarters, C a half and D a quarter. No evidence changed. Google DeepMind's score moves from 7% to 4% because its "Safe internal channel" grade is a D. The evaluator tab is graded the same way, and Anthropic's score there moves from 42% to 33%.

entry.title: Google DeepMind: Google says new hires' non-disparagement terms no longer apply after they leave
entry.summary: Google told the Washington Post on 3 November that it had recently removed "the post-termination aspect of non-disparagement clauses" from its terms for new hires, and that it doesn't enforce non-disparagement clauses after people leave. "No gag on criticism" now cites this and stays "Falls short": Google only described removing the part that applies after someone leaves, it didn't say existing contracts had changed, and the new wording isn't public. If Google publishes the wording, it will be rated on that wording. Scores are unchanged.

entry.title: New beta tab: what's public about labs' contracts with outside evaluators
entry.summary: A second tab rates what's public about each lab's contracts with third-party evaluators, using the six terms in GovAI's proposal that these contracts be published: scope, access, publication rights, pay, conflict rules, and term and renewal. Anthropic scores 42% and OpenAI 33%, mostly "Partly" from their own announcements; Google DeepMind, xAI and Meta score 0% because nothing is public. No lab has published a full evaluation contract. These scores are separate and don't change the staff-contract scores.

entry.title: Google DeepMind: a former researcher posts the non-disparagement clause he signed
entry.summary: Andreas Kirsch, a former Google DeepMind research scientist, posted on X a clause from the agreement he signed with Google in the UK in 2024. It says staff must not make "any statement" "criticising or disparaging Google", during or after employment, and he says it has no exemption for protected disclosures. "No gag on criticism" now cites it as its main source and stays "Falls short". A new entry for "Protected disclosures carved out" stays "Not public", because the rest of the agreement isn't public. Scores are unchanged.

entry.title: Lab Canary launched
entry.summary: Five labs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, xAI and Meta) rated on public evidence against seven clauses.
